title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.20116v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in settings where textual summaries, numerical observations, and external tool outputs may provide conflicting evidence. We study how LLMs arbitrate between such sources when they support opposing decisions. To do so, we introduce a controlled synthetic benchmark in which latent risk trajectories generate both numerical time series and natural language summaries, allowing us to construct conflicts where exactly one evidence source is aligned with the ground-truth label. This design lets us independently manipulate modality, temporal recency, source reliability, and evidence provenance. Across open-weight instruction-tuned models, we find that arbitration behaviour is systematic rather than random: models exhibit distinct text-versus-number preferences, follow temporal recency more consistently than explicit reliability cues, and can over-rely on external forecasts even when they conflict

translated_title: 当文本与数字不一致：大型语言模型中的证据仲裁
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于文本摘要、数值观察和外部工具输出可能提供相互冲突证据的场景中。我们研究了当这些来源支持相反决策时，LLMs如何在这些来源之间进行仲裁。为此，我们引入了一个受控的合成基准，其中潜在风险轨迹生成数值时间序列和自然语言摘要，使我们能够构建出恰好有一个证据来源与真实标签一致的冲突。这种设计让我们能够独立地操控模态、时间新近性、来源可靠性和证据出处。在开放权重的指令调优模型中，我们发现仲裁行为是系统性的而非随机的：模型表现出明显的文本与数字偏好，对时间新近性的遵循比对显式可靠性线索更一致，并且即使外部预测与内部证据冲突，模型也可能过度依赖外部预测。
tldr: 本文通过合成基准研究大型语言模型在文本与数值证据冲突时的仲裁行为，发现模型系统性偏好时间新近性而非可靠性线索，并可能过度依赖外部预测。
en_tdlr: This paper studies how large language models arbitrate between conflicting textual and numerical evidence using a synthetic benchmark, finding systematic preferences for temporal recency over reliability cues and potential over-reliance on external forecasts.
